content.page_title: 8.2 Clinical characteristics of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction / 8.3 The diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
content.section_8.2_summary: HFpEF differs from HFrEF and HFmrEF: HFpEF patients are older and more often female. Atrial fibrillation (AF), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and non-cardiovascular comorbidities are more common in HFpEF than in HFrEF. There are numerous potential causes of HFpEF and distinct pathophysiologies requiring different therapies.
red_flags_and_findings_suggesting_specif: Low or low-normal blood pressure in patients with history of hypertension
Intolerance to beta-blockers or ACE inhibitors (ACE-I)
History of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome
Echocardiographic features: thickening of septum, posterior wall, or RV wall
content.section_8.3_diagnostic_summary: Diagnosis of HFpEF is challenging. Multiple diagnostic criteria exist with varying sensitivity and specificity. Two score-based algorithms (H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF) have been proposed and widely tested, but diagnostic performance varies and many patients are classified as intermediate likelihood.
content.diagnostic_scores_notes: Both H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF assign a substantial proportion of suspected HFpEF patients to intermediate likelihood, requiring additional testing. Access to specialized tests may be limited, reducing broad applicability.
recommended_simplified_pragmatic_approac: Distil common major elements from prior diagnostic criteria emphasizing widely available variables.
Use frequently available clinical and echocardiographic variables as pivot points beyond which CV mortality risk is increased.
simplified_diagnostic_steps_listed: 1. Symptoms and signs of heart failure
content.references_to_consensus_and_position_sta: Recommendation consistent with consensus document of the HFA and ESC/HFA position statement; refers readers to full diagnostic approach recommended by HFA for clinicians with access to expertise.
